search_log: Searched “Stephen King Cell novel excerpt Clay Riddell first chapter publisher” and opened the Simon & Schuster authorized excerpt.

Searched “Cell Stephen King point of view third person narrator,” “Cell by Stephen King third person,” and related narrative-perspective variants; opened an explicit whole-book description of third-person narration with Clay as focal character.
Searched the exact text of q00298, q00307, q00308, and q00309 to resolve pronoun attribution and lost quotation boundaries; this confirmed that q00307 and q00309 are character speech.

Checked Stephen King’s official work page, Hachette, Fresh Fiction, Guardian, and Google Books-oriented results for excerpts, framing, or alternating-person evidence. Synopses and digested retellings were nondiagnostic, and no credible evidence of sustained first-, second-, or alternating-person sections was found.
person_note: The base narrator is nonparticipating third person, closely focalized mainly through Clay. Several interior Goodreads passages independently expose external narration and access to characters’ thoughts, agreeing with the authorized opening and the explicit whole-book POV description. The isolated “we” in q00298 is inclusive rhetoric about surviving humanity, not a sustained first-person section; q00307 and q00309 are local speech, and the opening’s “you” is reader address. No credible contrary or alternating structure was found.
